**VPC Lattice Resource Gateway ≠ PrivateLink endpoint.** The Resource Gateway is an ENI in your subnets for private **egress** to VPC targets; the PrivateLink VPC endpoint is for **ingress** to AgentCore. The Accelerator warns explicitly: "Customers should not conflate these two constructs." Mixing them up produces security groups that block the wrong direction.

Caching guardrail decisions is high-risk and should be tightly constrained if used at all: guardrail evaluation is non-deterministic, AWS auto-updates the underlying models, and "similar" inputs can differ exactly in the attack payload. If you cache, restrict it to **exact-match inputs only, with a short TTL, and never for the prompt-attack category**.

The largest billable family (300–1000-trial sweeps) and the one that changes engine mode to LOG_ONLY and back. The mode change is restored and the restoration is verified by a guard, but a re-run that dies between the two leaves the engine in LOG_ONLY, so an unattended run needs the restore step owned by the state machine rather than by the producer.

F5 grants and revokes IAM permissions, authors SCPs, and attaches permissions boundaries in order to demonstrate a bypass and then close it. A scheduler that could do this could also leave it done. The prohibition is not enforced by this flag — the flag states it; the enforcement is that no tool the director holds can express an F5 run at all.

Standard tier's mandatory cross-Region inference keeps data within the same geography (e.g., US requests stay in US Regions) at no extra cost, but "your input prompts and output results might move outside of your primary Region" — reconcile this with data-residency commitments and with the Guardrails-in-policy Regional constraint in Section 1.

F4 deliberately puts the policy engine into states in which it denies all traffic, to establish that it does. Those states are correct for the measurement and wrong for anything else sharing the account, and the exit condition is a restore whose failure is not observable from outside the run. A human approves the run and watches the restore.

Every F6 estimator is a paired difference of wall clocks measured at the client. The quantity is therefore a property of the client's network position as much as of the service: the same guardrail measured from an in-region EC2 instance and from a laptop over the public internet produces two different numbers, neither of which is wrong.

The spine runs top to bottom in request order; a box to the right of a spine box is a property of it — what it costs, how long it takes, whether it is repeatable, whether you can see it work.

AgentCore's architecture provides an out-of-process enforcement point at the Gateway data plane, which the Accelerator describes explicitly: "Policies intercept all agent traffic at the gateway boundary and **cannot be bypassed by agents or malicious actors**" (Accelerator v2.9, Policy section).

AWS periodically and automatically updates the underlying guardrail models ("Updates apply automatically and require no action on your part"). Maintain a regression test set and re-validate guardrail behavior on a schedule — past evaluation results do not guarantee future behavior.

There is no pass rate in this report. Of this study's published verdicts, 23 are FALSE and 20 are INCONCLUSIVE; a ratio would treat 'measured, and the guidance did not hold' as the same kind of miss as 'nothing was established', and would count a control never examined as a pass.

**Goal:** enforce a "hook" on EVERY tool use by the agent — analogous to PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks in agent frameworks — such that the agent runtime **cannot skip, bypass, or disable the hook itself**, even if the model is prompt-injected or the agent code is compromised.

A replication must hold the client fixed and vary only the day, so an F6 re-run from anywhere other than the original MacBook is a NEW measurement and may not be compared with day 1. The platform may prepare a run bundle and ingest the results; it must never trigger the run.

The gateway declares `authorizerType: NONE`. This study measured nothing about inbound authentication, so it has no verdict to offer here — which is not the same as finding no problem. `NONE` is a real value in the service model and its consequences are yours to assess.

measured_on: see the file name; this script takes no clock reading

what_each_count_is_not.artifact_strings_also_present_in_a_curat: The rule's own blind spot, counted rather than argued about: a curation file that quotes an artifact verbatim classifies as ARTIFACT, so this many strings could belong in either category and only a human reading them can say which.
what_each_count_is_not.identifier_nodes_not_marked_lang_en_on_t: Published so the split above is auditable, and NOT filed as a defect: a digest or a path is pronounced character by character in either language and its glyphs do not differ between the two font stacks, so marking it changes nothing a reader perceives.
what_each_count_is_not.payload_strings_of_prose_length: Not a backlog. It includes every string the payload carries at any path, most of which no component reads.
what_each_count_is_not.producers_the_backlog_traces_to: Not a file count and not a task count. One key can be a template in a program (`audit.json/markdown` is composed by platform/audit/report.py) or a literal in a curation file; the key says where to look, not how much work is behind it.
what_each_count_is_not.quoted_prose_nodes_not_marked_lang_en_on: Not part of the translation backlog and not fixed by translating anything: these sentences are correctly English. The defect is that the markup does not say so, so a screen reader on the zh-TW page applies Mandarin phonology to them and the CJK font fallback picks the wrong glyph forms. Counted here because only a DOM walk that knows which strings are quoted can see it; the invariant harness holds a floor on lang="en" elements, which detects collapse but cannot say the right ones are marked.
what_each_count_is_not.quoted_prose_nodes_that_do_carry_lang_en: The denominator for the count above, and the only thing that makes a zero there readable. It is not a quality measure: it says the whole-node match CAN fire, so a zero unmarked count means the marks are present rather than that the probe is blind.
what_each_count_is_not.rendered_and_an_identifier_not_prose: Not a backlog and not a provenance claim. A digest, an ARN, a resource id or a `results/phase1/*.json` path has no words, so it is owed no translation and no `lang` marking; this count exists so those strings are visibly EXCLUDED from the backlog rather than quietly dropped from it. It says nothing about whose bytes they are.
what_each_count_is_not.rendered_and_artifact: Not work. These are a producer's or the pre-registration's own words and must stay English, marked lang="en". Translating them would make this platform a paraphrase layer over its own evidence.
what_each_count_is_not.rendered_authored_and_identical_in_both_: The backlog, and the only count here that is one. A string in this set is this platform's own prose that a zh-TW reader reads in English.
